tagline: Know what your scans can't see — before you trust them.
lore: Chronos, the embodiment of time — here he measures where your scans spend their time, and how much of the estate they actually see.
problem: Every dashboard and priority list is only as good as the scans underneath it. An uncredentialed host reports a fraction of its real findings, a failed login looks like a clean host, and an old scan quietly ages the data — and nobody notices until a "clean" asset turns out to have been half-blind.
does: Chronos reads Tenable's scan-information and credential-status plugins to show which assets were scanned with a working login, which were blind and why, how fresh each scan is, which crown jewels sit in a blind spot, and how scanners, policies and scans perform. Every set can be tagged so the fix gets routed.

glance.caption: Chronos's At a glance on a 128-asset lab: 57 of 128 assets credentialed (44.5%) — 4 credential failures, 67 scanned without credentials, 3 credentialed with a credential issue; every scan over 90 days old; all 58 crown jewels (ACR ≥ 7) in a blind spot; average scan 7m 20s and scanner load.

capabilities: credentialed = the scan-information plugin reports credentialed checks, or a valid-credentials plugin is present; blind = scanned without credentials. Every hound in the pack uses this rule.
credential failed, insufficient privilege, intermittent, or no credentials at all — and credentialed hosts that still have a credential issue.
scanned in the last 7 days, 8–30, 31–90, over 90, never, or date unknown; network vs agent scans.
crown jewels (ACR ≥ 7) that are uncredentialed or failed, or not scanned in over 90 days.
average scan time, slow scans, slow scanners, policies and scans; scanner load; scanners on an old plugin feed; safe-checks scans.

Cred Failure, Insufficient Privilege, Intermittent Auth, Uncredentialed, Patch Assessment Failed, Stale Scan 30d+ / 90d+, Never Scanned, Slow Scan, Crown Jewel Blind Spot, and by scanner, policy or scan.
how: Chronos reproduces `navi scan evaluate` over your local navi.db — no extra scanning. The rule exactly: plugin 19506 says "Credentialed checks : yes", or plugin 141118 or 110095 is present. The asset list pages and filters on the server and exports to CSV. Tagging re-runs the evaluation on the server and tags the exact assets under Scan Health, behind the write gate and a confirm.
who: Scan engineers tuning credentials, scanners and policies, and VM leads who want to know how much of the estate their numbers actually describe.
better: Chronos's rule decides "blind" for the whole pack — Nemesis's confidence, Janus's coverage, Fenrir's uncredentialed hosts, Alert Raven's coverage alert and On the Scent's funnel. Amarok's credential test tells you why a login fails, and Covenant re-applies the Scan Health tags on its schedule.
cta: Ask Chronos what your scans are missing — trust is measured, not assumed.
